architecture.title: One policy enforcement point, five checks, in order
architecture.caption: Every tool call in the Hotel Ops Ensemble passes one policy enforcement point (Ensemble.authorize) carrying the origins of the text that asked for it. The checks run in order: least agency (may this agent hold the tool?) → parameter bounds (is the value safe?) → principal authorisation (may the least-trusted origin ask for it?) → egress (may data go there?) → a human for critical tools. A delegation keeps its origins, so a hop cannot launder a guest's request into a colleague's.

sequence.title: A03 with least agency vs with provenance-based authorisation
sequence.caption: With tool_allowlist on, the concierge cannot touch room setpoints, so it delegates; the energy agent holds the tool and obeys (captured in Lab 05-1/05-2). With principal_authz on, the same call still carries the origin guest:1203, and principal_rule refuses it because guest 1203 may act only on room 1203 (captured in Lab 05-2).

charts.title: Attacks blocked by each Module 05 control (A01–A05, A11)
charts.caption: From Lab 05-3 step 4, captured on this Mac with the SIM brain (a teaching model of a gullible LLM, not a measurement of a real one). A11 always runs with a rubber-stamp human, so HITL stops only A01 here. Least agency stops nothing because every attack reaches the agent that holds the tool.
